description.value:
These mysterious beings, often known as the Aeternae, are outsiders from a different plane of existence born from the weave of the world's aether.

Standard Racial Traits

  • Ability Score Modifiers: Immortals gain a +2 racial bonus to one ability score of their choice at creation.
  • Type: Immortals are Humanoid creatures with the immortal subtype.
  • Size: Immortals are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.
  • Base Speed: Immortals have a base speed of 30 feet.
  • Languages: Immortals begin play speaking Common. Immortals with high Intelligence scores can choose from: Celestial, Draconic, Galkan, Goblin, Lalafellan, Mithran, and Orc.

Defense Racial Traits

  • Immunity to Death: Immortals are immune to death effects and spells.
  • Immunity to Undeath: Immortals are immune to effects that would raise them as undead.

Feat and Skill Racial Traits

  • Integrated: Immortals gain a +1 racial bonus on Bluff, Disguise, and Knowledge (local) checks.
  • Long-Lived: Immortals can select up to four Knowledge skills as class skills.
  • Sociable: When immortals fail a Diplomacy check by 5 or more, they can try to influence the creature a second time even if 24 hours have not passed.

Magical Racial Traits

  • Linking: Once per day, immortals can link with a non-immortal spellcaster to cast 1 spell from their known list as a spell-like ability.

Other Racial Traits

  • Immortal: Immortals do not age past just before middle age, and are immune to aging effects.
  • Spirit-Tapped: When negative hit points reach their Constitution score, they gain a permanent negative level instead of dying.
  • Undying: Immortals automatically stabilize at -1 hit points or lower.

Weakness Racial Traits

  • Magic Ineptitude: Immortals cannot obtain a magic pool nor use spell-trigger/completion items except through Linking.
  • Not of this Plane: Immortals are vulnerable to dispel checks and anti-magic fields, and are affected by spells targeting outsiders/summoned creatures.
